newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Email sees improvement alongside profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Email sees improvement alongside profit rise.

text.p: Manufacturer Email Ltd said on Thursday that it expected a second year of higher net profits in 1997/98 after achieving A$58.7 million (US$44.61 million) in the year to March 31.
This compared with a net profit before abnormal items of A$53.3 million in the previous year.

Email, which struggled during the early to mid-1990s as Australia came out of a recession characterised by weak consumer spending, said demand during the final 1996/97 quarter was appreciably stronger for its metals group and major household appliances.
"However, demand since balance date has been more in line with the subdued climate of the previous year," it added.
The effects of much-predicted upturns in both residential and commercial building had been slow to appear.
"The company is expecting further improved results in 1997/98, based on the internal cost, quality and performance initiatives in place," it said.

The degree of improvement would depend upon the prevailing economic conditions. The government has forecast that Australia would achieve economic growth of 3.75 percent in 1997/98 from 3.25 percent in 1996/97.
Sales rose to A$2.21 billion from A$2.12 billion.
Email said profit before tax and goodwill amortisation rose 31.8 percent to A$94.0 million.
Tax almost doubled to A$29.12 million, while goodwill amortisation more than doubled to A$6.2 million following the acquisition of Atlas Steels.
